876331|"Set to 0" → 0; "change by 1" adds 1 to the existing number → 0 + 1 = 1.
7df6a8|A variable = a box with a name

2643e8|

A variable is a box with a name that holds a number that can change. Give the box a name (like score or distance), and the program can later "open it and look" or "replace it with a new number".

Like a scoreboard: it starts at 0 and grows with each point.
67588c|Two common blocks: set and change

8dfe30|
  • set score to (0): swap the box's contents straight to 0. (set)
  • change score by (1): add 1 to the existing number. (change)
82a421|"Change by 1" is not "become 1"! It adds 1 to the existing number. To make it exactly 1, use "set to".
33e77b|Variables can go inside blocks

ade6cd|

84428c|My Blocks: wrap a group of actions

530e5d|

A "My Block" lets you wrap a commonly used group of blocks into one new block, give it an easy name, and call it directly. For example, wrap [forward 200 → turn right 90] as "walk one side".

You can make one by pressing "Make a Block" in the My Blocks category.
e9ff04|Benefits: reuse, change in one place

16e5e0|

The program gets shorter and easier to read. More importantly: when you need to change something (say the angle is inaccurate), you only edit inside the block once and every place that calls it takes effect — nothing gets missed.

6f2bc2|

8867c4|Five steps of debugging

288d5a|
  1. Observe: what exactly is wrong? (How many mm off? How many degrees?)
  2. Guess the cause: what could it be?
  3. Change only one thing at a time
  4. Retest: test several times, don't trust one run.
  5. Record: write it in the engineering notebook.

b3e0ec|A robot often drifts slowly when it should go straight. What's a better fix?

766435|Feedback means "measure, notice the drift, correct", repeated again and again.
668689|Why does it drift?

8d3eff|

The left and right motors and wheels can't have exactly the same speed, so it slowly drifts as it goes. The drift builds up as it goes.
c804c4|Feedback: measure, compare, correct

fbee2a|

Use the Gyro to measure the current heading and compare with the target: error = target − current. Then adjust the difference between the left and right wheel speeds according to the error to pull the robot back. This must be done inside a repeat all the time.
aeec78|P control: correction = Kp × error

affbba|

The simplest approach: the correction is proportional to the error. A big error gives a big correction; a small error gives a small one. Kp decides how strong the correction is.

  • Kp too small: can't pull it back, still drifts.
  • Kp just right: returns to the line smoothly.
  • Kp too big: swings left and right (oscillation).

fe25ae|Odometry: estimate position from how much the wheels turned

e6de25|

Odometry uses how many turns the wheels made to work out "how far the robot went and how much it turned", with no extra sensor.
0b3f2d|Two formulas

03ba00|

Forward = (left wheel distance + right wheel distance) ÷ 2
Turn angle = (right − left) ÷ wheel track (radians)

Equal on both sides = straight; the right wheel going farther = turning left.
8698f2|Errors build up

20b95d|

Wheel slip, an uneven mat and tiny wheel-diameter errors — these small errors add up at every step, so the longer it goes, the less accurate it is. That's why it's often paired with the Gyro to correct heading.
